summary: Assess wave and tidal resources, compare technologies and shape project plans. Explore this practical marine renewable energy training course.
lede: Marine energy assessment helps project developers, coastal planners and energy engineers evaluate ocean-power opportunities and screen potential sites. Participants practise reviewing wave and tidal resource data, comparing converter options, and considering grid access, coastal uses, costs and project risks. They also learn to identify evidence gaps and present feasibility findings to support early project decisions, without undertaking detailed marine engineering design.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals involved in early-stage ocean power assessment, project planning, infrastructure decisions and public-sector energy programmes. It is designed for practitioners who need to assess feasibility and coordinate technical evidence, rather than perform detailed marine engineering design.
modules: GIS Site Screening and Coastal Uses
prerequisites: Familiarity with renewable energy project stages, energy systems or coastal infrastructure is recommended. No coding is required. You will use spreadsheet calculations for indicative comparisons; detailed marine survey or engineering-design experience is not required.
